stories.headline: At least 5 dead after powerful 7.7 earthquake hits Indonesia's Flores island
stories.title: At least 5 dead after powerful 7.7 earthquake hits Indonesia's Flores island
stories.summary: Jakarta, August 15 : At least five people were killed after a powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake hit off the coast of Indonesia's Flores Island on Saturday morning. CNN reported the confirmed death toll, citing updates from Provincial Police Chief Rudi Darmoko to regional media. The main tremor struck around 6 AM local time roughly 68 kilometres northwest of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara province and was followed by a series of aftershocks, CNN reported, citing data from the US Geological Survey (USGS). The USGS estimated that about 500,000 people were exposed to very strong or severe shaking, which damaged buildings and shocked residents awake, forcing them to flee their homes. Indonesia's national disaster mitigation agency, BNPB, noted that an initial tsunami warning was triggered following the quake but was later lifted. The agency added that about 2,000 residents in the Nagekeo regency evacuated as a precautionary measure. Early damage assessments from BNPB indicate that around 15 buildings, including personal homes and government offices, sustained damage, CNN reported. The developments follow a massive earthquake of magnitude 7.4 that jolted Indonesia early on Saturday, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS). The earthquake occurred at a depth of 49 km, the NCS said in a post on X."EQ of M: 7.4, On: 15/08/2026 03:28:24 IST, Lat: 8.557 S, Long: 121.181 E, Depth: 49 Km, Location: Indonesia," the NCS said. A tsunami warning was also issued after the massive earthquake, according to the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC). Soon after, another earthquake of magnitude 6.3 struck the Flores Sea, located between the Indonesian islands of Flores and Sulawesi, at a depth of 63 km. The tremor occurred at 3:43 am IST, according to the NCS. "EQ of M: 6.3, On: 15/08/2026 03:43:55 IST, Lat: 8.298 S, Long: 120.164 E, Depth: 63 Km, Location: Flores Sea," it said in another post. This was followed by a third earthquake of magnitude 6.0, which was recorded in the Flores Sea at a depth of 42 km at 3:58 am IST, the NCS said. "EQ of M: 6.0, On: 15/08/2026 03:58:41 IST, Lat: 8.494 S, Long: 121.601 E, Depth: 42 Km, Location: Flores Sea," the NCS posted on X. Indonesia is prone to frequent seismic and volcanic activity. (ANI)

stories.headline: NEADS and LIC HFL launch RAHAT project to aid 1,300 flood-hit families in Upper Assam
stories.title: NEADS and LIC HFL launch RAHAT project to aid 1,300 flood-hit families in Upper Assam
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: JORHAT: North-East Affected Area Development Society (NEADS), a local humanitarian organisation, in partnership with LIC Housing Finance Limited (LIC HFL), has launched emergency relief assistance for 1,300 flood-affected households across Charaideo and Sivasagar districts of Upper Assam under the LIC HFL RAHAT project.

The relief distribution was initiated in response to the continuing impact of floods across the two districts, which have disrupted household living conditions, food security, hygiene, and access to essential resources.
The RAHAT Project aims to provide timely and dignified humanitarian assistance to vulnerable families facing the immediate consequences of the floods.

The first-day distribution programme was held at Choladhara, Charaideo, in the presence of Abhinav Das, CSR Regional Lead (Northeast Zone), LIC Housing Finance Limited, along with the Chairperson of NEADS, members of the NEADS team, and the NEADS Emergency Response Team.

stories.headline: Situation across LoC vindicates 1947 decision: CM Omar
stories.title: Situation across LoC vindicates 1947 decision: CM Omar
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 15 : Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Saturday said that the situation across the Line of Control today has vindicated the decision taken by Jammu and Kashmir’s leaders 80 years ago was correct. Addressing the main Independence Day function at Bakshi Stadium in Srinagar, Omar as per the news agency—Kashmir News Observer (KNO), said “When I look across the border and across the LoC today, I realise that 80 years ago, the decision our leaders took for us was the right decision.” Omar said the people of Jammu and Kashmir resisted tribal raiders and infiltrators in 1947 even before the Indian Army reached the region. “Before the army of India arrived, the people of Jammu and Kashmir fought against the tribal raiders, fought against the infiltrators sent from across the border, and fought against the attackers,” he said. He said the slogan “Hamlawar Tayyar, Hum Kashmiri Hain Khabardaar” echoed across cities, villages, streets, and homes. “Those who had weapons used them. Those who did not have weapons showed fake guns and still fought against the infiltrators,” Omar added. The Chief Minister described the situation in the part of Jammu and Kashmir across the LoC as “sad” and “regretful.” “That part of Jammu and Kashmir is ours. We consider those people as our own, not strangers, not outsiders,” he said. He further remarked that had the situation in Jammu and Kashmir not changed in 2019, people across the LoC would have been protesting for reunification. “I realise that if our situation had not changed in 2019, then the people of that part of Jammu and Kashmir would have been protesting for us to reunite,” he said. Omar also pointed out that seats in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly continue to be kept vacant for representatives from those areas, with the hope that one day they will occupy them. Talking about federalism, Chief Minister Omar Abdullah said it should be strengthened by returning to Jammu and Kashmir what was snatched away. “When we talk about federalism, it should be strengthened from Jammu and Kashmir by returning to us what was taken away, so that federalism does not remain confined to words but is implemented in practice,” he said. Referring to the Jantar Mantar protests, the Chief Minister said the consequences of weakening federalism could often be witnessed on the streets. “The protest we saw on the streets of Delhi and at Jantar Mantar was a consequence of this. As per our federal list, education and health are the responsibility of the states and continue to remain so. But the examination pattern-through NEET and JEE-was created to snatch away the rights of the states to enroll students in colleges,” he said. Omar said Independence Day was not only a day of celebration but also an occasion for remembrance and introspection. “Today is a day of joy, a day of remembrance, a day of reflection,” he said. Referring to recruitment controversies in Jammu and Kashmir, Omar said allegations surrounding recruitment had forced young people to take to the streets. “The reality is, that to lose trust on something, or on a system, is a game of minutes. To regain trust, takes years and years,” he said. He called for admissions and recruitment processes in Jammu and Kashmir to be clear, transparent and merit-based. Omar said the government must maintain a continuous relationship with the people and work according to their expectations and circumstances. He also underlined the role of the opposition and media in a democracy, saying the government’s responsibility was to work, the opposition’s to hold it accountable and the media’s to hold both accountable. Omar assured the people of Jammu and Kashmir that his government would continue to represent and serve them and work towards fulfilling their aspirations. “On this occasion, I want to assure the people of Jammu and Kashmir that we are for you. We will continue to represent you. We will continue to serve you,” he said. He reiterated his government’s commitment to statehood, constitutional guarantees and development, saying it would work to fulfil the aspirations of the people and honour the sacrifices of those who fought for Jammu and Kashmir’s future. The Chief Minister congratulated the people on Independence Day and expressed hope that the next 80 years of the country would be more magnificent, advanced, fraternal and peaceful than the past 80 years—(KNO)

stories.headline: Borders Defines Indian: But Who Defines Border Citizen?
stories.title: Borders Defines Indian: But Who Defines Border Citizen?
stories.summary: As the 80 th anniversary of Independence Day dawns, the country will simply go into an overdrive with customary grandeur. The Tricolour will flutter atop important buildings; schoolchildren will sing patriotic songs, and speeches will extol the sacrifices that won us freedom from our colonial masters. A nation- state is defined by two of its very distinct facets—its people who populate its entire length and breadth and off course the national boundaries/borders. Both of these entities find ample space and discourse in its constitution and are complementary to each other. Not one of them individually can define the concept of a nation-state on its own steam. No wonder eighty years back, when Cyril Radcliffe the British lawyer cum boundary commission chairman set out his task of defining the national boundaries of India and Pakistan in a mere forty five days span , even he wouldn’t have realized the importance of carving out such a ‘cartographic lineation’. Since this lineation was followed by one of the biggest human displacements with bloody repercussions in modern times across the Radcliffe line, hence the uniqueness of this partition.The borders of a country are not merely ‘cartographic labyrinthine’ but a place where the republic is tested every single day. It is where the idea of India ceases to be an abstraction and becomes a lived reality. Ironically, while the border defines India’s geography, the ‘border citizen’ often remains invisible in India’s policymaking. For close to seventy nine years, India has viewed its national borders primarily through the prism of military strategy, investing in troops, weapons, surveillance and other infra to protect its territorial integrity. These investments are indispensible no doubt, but they also reveal a deeper flaw in our national thinking right from 1947. We have treated borders as military spaces to be defended rather than living spaces to be nurtured. This distinction matters, and hence my endeavour to pen down this write up on India’s 80 th Independence day to put under the scanner such a distinction which may not portend well for our country if left untreated. A nation-state is not merely secured by its armed forces guarding its borders. It is secured when citizens choose to live there with dignity, confidence and hope. Every inhabited village on the border is a declaration of national sovereignty. Every family that refuses to abandon its ancestral home despite enemy shelling, infiltration or isolation is performing an act of national service that rarely finds mention from the ramparts of Red fort of India. Nowhere is this reality more visible than in Jammu & Kashmir. Border residents have lived through wars since 1947, terrorist violence, repeated ceasefire violations and prolonged uncertainty. Children have grown up distinguishing mortar fire from festival fireworks, farmers have cultivated fields under the shadow of sniper fire and many more such vagaries as thrown up by our inimical western neighbour at us. These are not isolated tragedies. But represent a way of life that few Indians living hundreds of Kilometers away can fully comprehend. Out of a stated fifteen thousand kilometers of total land boundary of India touching seven neighbouring nations, how much of border is actually under fire of ours? I may dare say only that which abuts our western neighbour in the UT of J&K and now under an uneasy calm punctuated by repeated ceasefire violations. Isn’t it suitable time on the anvil of 80 th Independence Day of India, that these hapless people are not left to the mercy of geo-political machinations of this sub-continent which are played with utter disregard to their wellbeing? Be that as it may, yet public policy frequently views border districts through the lens of relief rather than resilience. Compensation is announced after damage, roads are sanctioned after strategic necessity arises. Same is the case with a plethora of welfare schemes involving schools, hospitals and employment opportunities. In the after math of mayhem unleashed by Pakistan last year during ‘Op Sindoor’ on our border villages abutting both the IB and the LC, stories of continued neglect, administrative cum bureaucratic apathy emanate from media circles regarding laggardly pace of redevelopment of damaged infra. Leave alone relief, resilience is a far cry for us to come on top of the things as they stand today. The contrast with China is instructive. Both India & China threw out the yolk of slavery in the late 1940s. With a gap of only two years in between i.e. 1947 and 1949 respectively, China has pursued an integrated border strategy in which civilian settlements, economic development and military preparedness reinforce each other thereby surpassing India both in thought and action. Many of the readers of my article may argue that being a totalitarian cum communist nation, for China the concept of a nation-state supersedes its denizens. This is passé, simple and straight. For the sake of argument even if I do take this concept as viable, then may I ask why India has woken up lately to emulate the same concept in the format of VVP (Vibrant village programme now? The villages of China all along the LAC in our context present themselves the ‘Chinese instrument of national security, signaling that the writ of mandarins of power in Beijing runs not only in their national capital but right till the last village of theirs. Though India as stated above has lately started in the right earnest to rectify decades of its inertia in such matters, by kicking starting programmes like the VVP it is too late and too less. The intent though commendable, the scheme doesn’t inspire that much confidence. As late as few weeks back the PM in one of his discourses with the youth of India under the aegis of DIYLD (Developed India young leader’s dialogue) presented an idea before them of visiting border villages, stay and connect with them instead of using the virtual media to do so. This suggestion by our honourable PM throws an interesting question instead—‘Is merely encouraging the youth of India to visit these border villages enough? Can these cosmetics change the dismal situation as found present in these frontier areas? I shall not dwell much upon this topic, since it is being tackled by me in a separate article from Rising Kashmir paper. Border citizens per se ought to be placed head and shoulders above the rest of populace of our country. Their defining attributes being derived from their very stay in the border areas and acting as the sentinels of a democratic dispensation in a region surrounded by theocratic countries. As India enters its eightieth year of independence, perhaps the time is ripe enough to redefine the citizenry of our border areas who away from the din of the mainstream living of India are silently carving out an existence for themselves based on true values of nationalism. The strength of a nation cannot be measured in terms of its military or economic might. But from the confidence of its citizens living at its farthest edge. If the border defines India’s territorial identity, then the ‘border citizens’ defines its moral identity. How India treats those who stand at its frontiers reveals what kind of republic it truly is. (The writer is a retired army officer and a regular scribe of Rising Kashmir. He can be approached on his email: slalotra4729@gmail.com)

stories.headline: Supreme Court stays Madras HC order striking down compassionate appointments for Karur stampede victims’ kin
stories.title: Supreme Court stays Madras HC order striking down compassionate appointments for Karur stampede victims’ kin
stories.summary: Justice J.B. Pardiwala asked what was wrong with the government reaching out to give “some succour to the families who have suffered such a tragedy”
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Madurai Bench of the High Court had quashed the government orders granting jobs to the victims’ family members on compassionate grounds on July 27.
Justice J.B. Pardiwala asked what was wrong with the government reaching out to give “some succour to the families who have suffered such a tragedy”.
“Don’t bring politics into this, such stampede took place several people died.
If the government has decided to give jobs, then who are the respondents to oppose it...

If sole member has died in the stampede, then there is nobody else in the family who is earning, should the government not give some employment to son or daughter or wife according to their educational qualifications?” Justice Pardiwala observed orally.
The Judge said in many families the only bread winner may have perished in the stampede.

A total of 41 people died and around 100 others were injured in the crowd crush and stampede on September 27, 2025 during a Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) roadshow addressed by current Chief Miniter Joseph Vijay, who is also the party president.
The State had argued in the court that the appointments were meant as a humane gesture.
But the court concluded that specific guidelines covered the field of compassionate appointments, and they cannot be cast aside by the State government.
The High Court had warned that the government’s action, if condoned, may run the risk of opening the floodgates.
The High Court had pointed out that there were wait-lists in every government department for appointments on compassionate grounds.
Employment has to be granted only in accordance with seniority and not with reference to the immediate nature of relief to be granted, the Division Bench of the High Court had noted.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Has Duty To Decide Matters Of National Importance Soon : Justice KM Joseph Suggests Permanent Constitution Bench
stories.title: Supreme Court Has Duty To Decide Matters Of National Importance Soon : Justice KM Joseph Suggests Permanent Constitution Bench
stories.summary: Justice Joseph raised concerns over the delay in deciding matters such as defection.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Justice Joseph raised concerns over the delay in deciding matters such as defection.

Former Supreme Court judge Justice K.M. Joseph has suggested that a permanent and regular Constitution Bench may be constituted in the Top Court, as an institutional reform, to decide on important issues in the country.
Justice Joseph made the suggestion while speaking at event organised by the Kerala High Court Advocates' Association (KHCAA) and the Constitution Debate Club.

Justice Joseph delivered a lecture on the topic 'Liberty Across Continents: The Enduring Legacy of the American Declaration of Independence & the Constitution of India' in the event held to commemorate the 250th Anniversary of the United States Declaration of Independence.

The suggestion to have a permanent Constitutional Bench was made while pointing out the long pendency of important matters, including a reference made in 2016 on the question as to whether courts can dictate timelines to a Speaker when deciding anti-defection petitions.
Justice Joseph quoted a few examples in different States, where there was inordinate delay on the side of the Speaker in deciding these petitions.
"Look at our country.
Look at the amount of defection that is taking place is our country.
Everybody in this country should be shocked at what is happening.
We do not know about where the truth lies – we hear about 'carrot and sticks', we hear about the ED being used, we hear about large sums of money being pumped out.
It happened in Maharashtra, it happened earlier also.
It is happening right in front of our eyes.

stories.headline: 'Should India Remain Underdeveloped?' : Supreme Court Slams Union's Opposition To Adopt Global Norms On Food Package Labelling
stories.title: 'Should India Remain Underdeveloped?' : Supreme Court Slams Union's Opposition To Adopt Global Norms On Food Package Labelling
stories.summary: "The World should know that India is very much concerned about the overall health of its citizens, more particularly the growing children," the Court said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: "The World should know that India is very much concerned about the overall health of its citizens, more particularly the growing children," the Court said.

The Supreme Court recently disapproved of the Union's stand that it can't follow international standards when it comes to issuing interpretative warnings of high sugar, sodium or fat content on packaged food items.
The Court questioned if India should remain underdeveloped, ignoring that obesity remains a significant public health concern.

The observations were made in the context of the failure of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to implement the Front-of-Package labelling (FOPL), a standard adopted at the international level.
It may be recalled that the Court on February 10 observed that FSSAI failed to file a satisfactory affidavit on mandatory compliance with FOPL.
It directed them to file another compliance report, and the matter was then taken up on August 13 before a bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran.

However, the Additional Solicitor General Brijender Chahar(for FSSAI) informed the bench that it can't comply with the FOPL as Indian dietary standards are different from those followed internationally.
This didn't sit well with the Court, which disapproved of the Union's stand that India can't match the standards of developed countries.
The Court observed: "We do not approve the stance of the Union when it says that it is not possible to match with international standards, more particularly, developed countries.
That's the question we are putting forward for the Union to consider.
The World should know that India is very much concerned about the overall health of its citizens, more particularly the growing children."
It reiterated that the matter concerns the health of the citizens, more particularly growing children whose health can't be compromised.

stories.headline: India in U.S. crosshairs again — White House report cites countries ‘enabling’ China’s tariff evasions
stories.title: India in U.S. crosshairs again — White House report cites countries ‘enabling’ China’s tariff evasions
stories.summary: The report has identified more than 40 countries associated with “elevated illegal transshipment risk”; the U.S. has named the Pune-Gujarat-Chennai belt as one of the areas enabling China
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India is once again in the U.S.’ crosshairs, this time for allegedly allowing China to evade U.S. tariffs by routing its exports through the country.
The latest allegations are part of a new White House report called ‘The Great Transhipment Scam’.
In particular, the U.S. has named the Pune-Gujarat-Chennai belt as one of the areas “enabling” China to evade tariffs to the detriment of supply chains in the U.S.

This comes at a time when the U.S. has already imposed a 10% tariff on India for not doing enough to stop the import of goods made using forced labour, and is in the process of enacting legislation that would see tariffs of up to 100% imposed on India for its import of Russian oil.
An ongoing investigation by the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) related to excess capacity could see further tariffs on top of all this.
The U.S. had in 2018 levied tariffs ranging from 7.5% to 100% on goods from China under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 for unfair trade and tech practices.
On July 24, 2026, it added a further 12.5% tariff for forced-labour compliance gaps.
“After their imposition, Chinese exporters increasingly routed goods through third countries,” the White House report noted.

“Products that previously moved directly from China to the United States were shipped through jurisdictions where limited assembly, finishing, repackaging, relabeling, or documentation changes could create the appearance of a different national origin.”
The report has identified more than 40 countries associated with “elevated illegal transshipment risk”, with India among the top “enablers” of China’s evasion of tariffs.
“The countries that comprise China’s Shadow Transshipment Network include many of America’s largest trading partners,” the report said.
“China’s biggest enablers range from Mexico and Canada on U.S. land borders to the European Union, India, Japan, and South Korea.”
